analysis.title: The S&P isn't listening: the great macro divide
key_insights: Bond volatility (MOVE) rose from 77 on September 10 to 113, back near the March panic highs, while SPX sits near record highs (about 7,700) and VIX barely moves.
The MOVE-to-VIX gap is at an extreme. Credit is pricing stress, and macro trading has migrated into fixed income.

GS says fixed-income ETF (FICC) option volume has more than doubled over three weeks, with traders using HYG, LQD, TLT and IEF instead of equity indices to express macro views. The 10-day average is roughly 2.2-2.4 million contracts.

GS says correlations between the S&P 500 and cross-asset signals (bonds, rates, oil, sentiment) have broken down. SPX implied vol is in the low double digits. GS desk: 'the equity market is trading the Fed, the bond market is trading the regime.'
Breadth is weak under the index. The spread between members making 52-week highs and lows has fallen to about -20, and index-to-sector correlations have fallen sharply.

GS's US Vol Panic Index is below 2/10 despite large rate and credit moves. The VIX to HYG implied vol ratio is at a 3+ year low, so credit options price more stress than equity options. GS says VIX upside convexity remains extremely attractive.

DB says financial stress no longer guarantees a central-bank rescue. Inflation is above target, unlike the 2010s. In 2022-23 (Ukraine, UK mini-budget, SVB) dovish repricing was followed by persistent inflation forcing central banks back toward tightening.

Persistent above-target inflation limits the central-bank response to market stress.

tension_points.bull_case: Options markets expect rates and credit stress not to spill materially into equities. SPX is near record highs with implied vol in the low double digits and the Vol Panic Index below 2/10.
tension_points.bear_case: MOVE at 113 and credit options pricing stress suggest equities are mispriced. Breadth is weak, and DB argues the Fed put is weaker with inflation above target.
